summaryText:
In the final message of the five-week series "My Wounds Won't Win," Pastor Travis Hearn invited the church to see that God can bring a comeback story out of brokenness. Opening with Proverbs 24:16, he reminded us that the righteous may fall, but they rise again. The enemy's goal is not only to knock us down, but to keep us down. Pastor Travis urged the congregation to stay walking, even when life changes the way we walk.

He built the message around three people who walked differently after encountering God. First, using Jacob's wrestling match in Genesis 32, he taught that some wounds do not stop your walk, but they do change it. Jacob had spent his life chasing the blessing instead of the Blesser. After his encounter with God he received a new name, Israel, and walked with a limp. Pastor Travis explained that the limp was not proof God had abandoned him, but proof he had met God. He emphasized that our wounds, weaknesses, and past failures are not our identity.

Second, through the story of Lazarus in John 11, he taught that some things were meant to defeat you, but because of God they could not keep you. When others said it was too late, Jesus called Lazarus out of the tomb. Jesus then told the people to take off the grave clothes and let him go. Pastor Travis challenged listeners that many believers have been set free but still wear shame, guilt, fear, bitterness, and old labels. Freed people do not need to keep dressing like prisoners.

Third, looking at Paul's thorn in 2 Corinthians 12, he taught that some things God removes and other things God redeems. Paul asked for removal, but God answered with grace that was sufficient. Pastor Travis shared briefly about his own serious health crisis in 2022 and the lasting effects he still lives with. He testified that God has used it for good, and that he is still walking. He also noted that the word for "rest on me" in 2 Corinthians 12:9 carries the picture of God's power making its home over our weakness.

The service closed with a prayer of surrender, an invitation to follow Jesus, and an encouragement to keep going in healing, forgiveness, and surrender after the series ends. The message of hope: your wounds may explain part of your story, but they do not get to determine your future.
mainPoints: Some wounds do not stop your walk, but they do change it. Like Jacob, we receive a new identity from God, and our wounds and weaknesses do not define us.
Some things were meant to defeat you, but because of God they could not keep you. Like Lazarus, we are called to take off the grave clothes of shame, guilt, fear, and bitterness and walk in freedom.
Some things God removes and other things God redeems. Like Paul's thorn, God's grace is sufficient, and His power makes its home over our weakness.

Monday.scripture: Proverbs 24:16 (NIV): "for though the righteous fall seven times, they rise again."
Monday.focus: Getting back up and still walking
Monday.action: Write down one area where you have felt knocked down. Then name one small step you can take today to keep walking, and text a trusted friend to ask for encouragement.
Monday.prayer: Lord, thank You that falling is not the end of my story. Help me rise again and keep walking with You today. Amen.

Tuesday.scripture: Genesis 32:28 (NIV): "Your name will no longer be Jacob, but Israel, because you have struggled with God and with humans and have overcome."
Tuesday.focus: My wound is not my identity
Tuesday.action: Write down one label from your past (spoken by others or by yourself). Next to it, write what God says about you. Read it aloud and thank Him for your new identity.
Tuesday.prayer: Father, You call me by Your name for me and not by my past. Help me to believe who You say I am. Amen.

Wednesday.scripture: 2 Corinthians 12:10 (NIV): "For when I am weak, then I am strong."
Wednesday.action: Choose one area where you have been trying to do everything on your own. Spend five minutes in quiet prayer handing it over to God, and ask Him to lead you in it.
Wednesday.prayer: Jesus, I come to the end of myself and lean on You. Be my strength where I am weak. Amen.

Thursday.scripture: John 11:44 (NIV): "Jesus said to them, 'Take off the grave clothes and let him go.'"
Thursday.action: Identify one grave cloth you still wear, such as shame, guilt, fear, bitterness, or offense. Write it on paper, pray over it, and then tear up or throw away the paper as a sign of release. If it is heavy, invite a trusted believer to pray with you.
Thursday.prayer: Lord Jesus, You have set me free. Help me lay down what You have already released me from and walk in freedom. Amen.

Friday.scripture: John 8:36 (NIV): "So if the Son sets you free, you will be free indeed."
Friday.action: Do one thing today that reflects freedom, such as forgiving someone in prayer, encouraging someone, or worshiping aloud with a song of praise. Share with a friend how God has helped you stay on your feet.
Friday.prayer: Father, thank You that the Son has made me truly free. Help me live today as someone who belongs to You. Amen.

Saturday.scripture: 2 Corinthians 12:9 (NIV): "My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness."
Saturday.focus: Trusting God's grace in the thorn
Saturday.action: Name one "thorn" you have asked God to remove. Pray the prayer of surrender from the sermon, trusting His grace. Then thank God for one way He has shown His faithfulness, and share it with someone who may need to hear it.
Saturday.prayer: God, I trust that Your grace is enough for me. Use my wounds for Your glory and make Your power at home in my weakness. Amen.

title: How to Keep Going When Life Hurts | I’m Still Walkin’
